READ-ONLY UX/PRODUCT AUDIT (do NOT edit files or run git/build/systemctl — analysis only). Audit the Nxeon VPS hosting platform at /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15). Read /opt/nxeon/CLAUDE.md, then review app/page.tsx, app/(marketing)/**, app/dashboard/**, app/admin/**, and components/** (customer, admin, marketing, portal, ui).

Assess as a product/UX reviewer for a premium cloud host (benchmark: DigitalOcean/Vercel/Hostinger):
- **Broken/dead-end flows**: buttons/links that go nowhere or 404, forms with no success/error/loading states, actions with no confirmation or feedback, empty states missing.
- **Customer vs admin consistency**: design-system drift, inconsistent components, pages that feel unfinished vs polished.
- **Missing obvious product surfaces**: things a VPS customer expects that aren't there (e.g. usage/billing history clarity, server rename, reverse DNS, alerts/notifications preferences, 2FA, team/org management, API keys/tokens for customers, referral program UI, knowledge base/docs, onboarding).
- **Deploy & lifecycle UX**: is the deploy wizard's flow sound (term selection, image requirements, add-ons)? Server management tabs completeness (console, metrics, snapshots, backups, networking, resize, activity). Resize/upgrade path clarity (does upgrading mid-term explain proration?).
- **Domain UX**: register wizard + dashboard + DNS manager quality.
- **Admin ops gaps**: anything a hosting operator needs that's missing (bulk actions, better search/filter, exports, per-node views, abuse handling UI, refunds, coupon/promo management).
- **Mobile responsiveness & accessibility** red flags (obvious ones from the markup: missing labels, tiny tap targets, non-responsive tables/grids, color-only status).
- **Copy/trust**: legal pages, pricing clarity, error message quality.

Output a findings list, each: [PRIORITY: high/medium/low] area — file/page — the gap or issue — why it matters — concrete suggestion. Group by: (1) Fix (broken/confusing), (2) Improve (polish/clarity), (3) Add (missing features). Lead with a short "top 10 things I'd change" summary. Be specific and reference real files.

1	# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform
2	
3	Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
8	- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
9	- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
10	- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
11	- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
12	- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).
13	
14	## Portals & design system
15	
16	- Customer portal (`app/dashboard/**`) and admin ops portal (`app/admin/**`) are separate sidebar apps sharing `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (sidebar, topbar, notifications bell, ⌘K command palette backed by `/api/search`).
17	- Design system lives in `app/globals.css` (glass cards, gradient buttons, navy palette) + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` + `components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free SVG charts). Use these — do not add chart libraries.
18	- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
19	- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners).
20	
21	## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)
22	
23	- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id).
24	- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
25	- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.
26	
27	## Conventions
28	
29	- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
30	- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
31	- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
32	- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
33	- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
34	
35	## Commands
36	
37	- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
38	- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker`
39	- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
40	- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
41	- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
42	
43	## Domains & TLS
44	
45	- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
46	- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
47	- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP.
48	- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.
49	
50	## Environments
51	
52	- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
53	- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080. Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
54	- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
55	- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at :8080 → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. The improvement agent should test changes on staging before promoting.
56	
57	## Safety rules
58	
59	- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
60	- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
61	- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
62	- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
63	- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
64	- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

I'm starting to compile the concrete gaps and issues I've spotted for the audit, and one major red flag stands out: the contact form has no actual backend implementation, just a mailto link, and it even displays a message to visitors saying the form lacks a backend with a placeholder support address. That's a significant trust and professionalism issue on a public-facing site.

The backups feature presents another mismatch—while the UI offers a "Create backup" button, restores require opening a support ticket, yet the marketing pages prominently claim users can "restore a server to any point in a couple of clicks." There are also several other marketing claims that don't align with what's actually in the product, like the repeated assertions about always-on DDoS mitigation and free WhoisGuard privacy on the domains page.

I'm also noticing inconsistencies around the domain registrar—the codebase references Namecheap but the app actually uses name.com, and the marketing copy mentions WhoisGuard (which is Namecheap's product) while the domain detail page shows a name.com DNS badge. The global infrastructure claims are similarly overstated—it's really just a single OVH server in Canada, not the globally distributed setup the marketing suggests.

The deploy wizard's add-ons section is also problematic—things like "daily auto-backups" are marked as included, which directly contradicts what I'm seeing in the backups tab where everything is manual and support-ticket dependent. I need to verify whether these add-ons actually function or if they're just cosmetic labels.

The pricing messaging is muddled too—the homepage says "save up to 20% with annual billing" but the VPS pricing page mentions "save up to 20% on 3-year terms," and domains have a different discount structure entirely. The terminology around "annual billing" versus actual commit terms (monthly/3-month/yearly/3-year options) is confusing throughout.

There are also some operational gaps in the admin interface: admins can power cycle, suspend, extend, or reset passwords on customer servers, but they can't manage port forwards, snapshots, backups, or resize instances on behalf of customers—which limits support capabilities. And there's no "view as customer" perspective either.

The invoice management is read-only with no way to refund, void, mark as paid, or create manual invoices, even though the system supports REFUNDED and VOID states. The billing system itself has no refund flow at all. There's also no coupon or discount management despite marketing claiming savings up to 20%—discounts are just hardcoded into the billing terms.

Admin tables like the users list lack pagination, which could become a scaling issue. And I notice there's no 2FA or MFA support anywhere in the product. But there's a major contradiction here: the networking setup uses NAT with shared IPv4 and port forwarding, yet marketing claims "Dedicated IPv4 address" on every plan—that's repeated about six times and it's a serious trust issue that needs fixing. Also missing: server rename functionality (hostname is locked after deployment), IPv6 support, and any way for customers to change their hostname.

Looking at the other gaps, there's no referral program mentioned, no knowledge base or documentation beyond support tickets, and the "isolated private networking" claim is misleading since the NAT /24 is actually shared across customers, not truly private. The deploy wizard itself works well with term selection on the review step and enforced image requirements, though the "popular" badge assignment is just based on plan index position rather than actual usage data. Add-ons section appears to be cut off.

On resizing, the UX explains the new price takes effect at renewal and mentions power cycling, but completely skips over proration — which is a real problem for prepaid terms. If someone's paid three years upfront and resizes to a bigger plan mid-term without proration explanation, they're essentially getting the upgrade for free until renewal. That's a significant billing gap that the interface doesn't address. There's also no downgrade path for disk.

The domain UX is solid overall — the registration wizard works well. The DNS manager lets you add and delete records but not edit them directly, which is a minor friction point. And pointing a domain at the box for web traffic only sets A records to the shared IP, so you'd need port forwarding on top of that, which the copy does mention but makes the whole flow feel clunky.

On mobile and accessibility, the wide tables mostly handle overflow well with scrolling containers and min-width constraints. The StatusDot component uses both color and text labels, which is the right call for accessibility.

The bandwidth meter combines color with percentage text and warning messages — good. Forms have proper labels throughout. The deploy wizard uses a mix of select dropdowns with aria-labels and custom radio buttons with visible text. The add-on toggles are styled spans rather than real checkboxes, but they're wrapped in buttons so they're still keyboard-accessible and clickable. The notifications dropdown has one quirk: clicking the bell marks all notifications as read immediately when you open it.

There are a few issues to flag: the about page has a visible placeholder banner that shouldn't ship, the contact form has a visible disclaimer, and there's a placeholder email address exposed publicly. The legal pages are mostly complete but note they should be finalized with legal counsel.

content.text:
I've completed a thorough read of the platform. Here is the audit.

---

# Nxeon UX / Product Audit

The platform is genuinely impressive: a coherent design system (`components/ui/primitives.tsx`, `charts.tsx`, glass/navy tokens), consistent loading/empty/error states across almost every surface, a strong deploy wizard, a real domain-registration flow, live metrics, and a deep admin ops console. It reads as 90% shippable. The gaps that remain are mostly **trust/accuracy of marketing claims vs. the actual NAT architecture**, a few **operator tooling holes**, and **visible placeholder text that must not ship**. Nothing is catastrophically broken.

## Top 10 things I'd change

1. **"Dedicated IPv4 on every plan" is false** — the architecture is shared-IP NAT with port forwards (20000–29999). Repeated across marketing. High trust/legal risk.
2. **"Isolated private networking" is overstated and a real tenancy concern** — all customer VMs share one L2 bridge/subnet (`10.20.0.0/24`, `vmbr1`). Not isolated per-customer.
3. **Ship-blocking placeholder text is visible to customers** — About page "Placeholder copy" banner, ContactForm "this form has no backend… placeholder" note, `support@nxeon.cloud`, Terms "finalized with legal counsel."
4. **Contact form doesn't submit** (`ContactForm.tsx` is `mailto:` only). Premium hosts don't do this.
5. **Backups over-promise vs. reality** — marketing says "restore in a couple of clicks"; product is manual-create + "open a support ticket to restore." The deploy "Daily auto-backups" add-on has no reflection in the Backups tab.
6. **Admin server detail lacks core operator tools** — no resize, snapshot, backup, port-forward management, or "view as customer" on behalf of a client.
7. **No refund / void / manual-invoice / mark-paid actions in admin** despite `REFUNDED`/`VOID` invoice statuses existing.
8. **Resize doesn't explain proration / mid-term billing** (explicitly asked). Prepaid multi-year customers can upsize for free until renewal.
9. **Missing expected VPS surfaces**: 2FA, customer API tokens (perpetually "coming soon"), team/org, server rename, notification/alert preferences.
10. **Pricing copy inconsistency** — homepage badge "Save up to 20% with annual billing" (20% actually needs a 3-year term); the `PricingGrid` badge promises savings with no term toggle on the page.

---

## (1) FIX — broken / confusing / misleading

**[HIGH] Trust/accuracy — "Dedicated IPv4" vs NAT** — `app/(marketing)/vps/page.tsx`, `features/page.tsx`, `domains/page.tsx`, `app/page.tsx`, `pricing/page.tsx` comparison tables, `components/marketing/PricingGrid.tsx`. Every VM sits behind NAT (`app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` Networking tab literally states "Your server sits behind NAT on a private network… public ports are forwarded"; SSH is `PUBLIC_IP:sshPort`). Marketing claims "dedicated IPv4 address" on every plan ~6 times. This is a material, repeated false claim. **Fix:** either provision real dedicated IPs or change copy to "shared IPv4 with dedicated forwarded ports / managed port forwarding," and drop "Dedicated IPv4" from the comparison tables.

**[HIGH] Security/trust — "isolated private networking"** — `features/page.tsx`, `vps/page.tsx`, `app/page.tsx` ("isolated NAT networking," "isolated private networking"). Per CLAUDE.md all VMs attach to the same `vmbr1` `10.20.0.0/24`. Customers share an L2 segment; it is not isolated per-tenant. **Fix:** stop claiming isolation, or implement per-customer VLANs/firewalling; at minimum this deserves a security review before the claim is public.

**[HIGH] Placeholder copy shipped to customers** — `app/(marketing)/about/page.tsx` renders an amber "**Placeholder copy.** …Replace before launch" banner; `components/marketing/ContactForm.tsx` renders "This form has no backend… Support address is a placeholder"; `app/legal/terms/page.tsx` ships "The specific governing jurisdiction should be finalized with legal counsel." **Fix:** gate these behind a launch flag or replace with real content. Visible "this is fake" text destroys trust on a paid product.

**[MED] Contact form is a dead end** — `components/marketing/ContactForm.tsx` only opens the visitor's mail client via `mailto:` and sets `sent=true` regardless of success. No delivery guarantee, no record. **Fix:** POST to a server action that creates a lead/ticket (the ticket infra already exists) with proper success/error states.

**[MED] Backups: marketing promise ≠ product** — `app/page.tsx` and `features/page.tsx` say "Restore a server to any recovery point in a couple of clicks," but `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` Backups tab offers only "Create backup" and tells users to "Open a support ticket with the backup name" to restore. Additionally the deploy wizard's "Daily auto-backups" add-on (`DeployWizard.tsx`, passed as `addon_backup`) never surfaces a schedule or "auto-backups: on" status in the Backups tab. **Fix:** add a self-service restore button, and show scheduled-backup status when the add-on is enabled — or soften the marketing copy.

**[MED] Registrar/brand copy inconsistency** — `app/(marketing)/domains/page.tsx` repeatedly promises "free **WhoisGuard** privacy" (WhoisGuard is Namecheap's product name), but the app registers via **name.com** (`app/admin/domains/page.tsx`, domain detail shows a "name.com DNS" badge; `NAMECOM_*` env). CLAUDE.md also references a `lib/namecheap.ts` that appears superseded by `lib/registrar.ts`. **Fix:** use a generic term ("free WHOIS privacy" — which the wizard already uses) and reconcile the dead Namecheap reference.

**[MED] "Global reach / built to scale out / low-latency infrastructure"** — `app/page.tsx` "Global reach" section + `GlobalNetwork` visual, `vps/page.tsx`. It's a single OVH box in one location; `app/admin/nodes/page.tsx` even notes cross-host networking isn't automatic. Overstated for a single-node deployment. **Fix:** tone down to "single high-performance location" until multi-region exists.

**[MED] Notifications mark-all-read on open + possible dead links** — `components/portal/Shell.tsx`: opening the bell calls `markNotificationsRead()` immediately, so the unread badge clears even if the user reads nothing; individual items link to `n.href ?? "#"` (a `#` no-op when href is null). **Fix:** mark read on item click (or on close), and hide/disable items without an href.

**[LOW] "popular"/"Most popular" badge is positional, not data-driven** — `PricingGrid.tsx` (`Math.floor((plans.length-1)/2)`) and `DeployWizard.tsx` (`i === Math.floor(plans.length/2)`). The two even use different formulas, so the "popular" plan can differ between marketing and the wizard. **Fix:** drive from a `plan.featured`/`popular` column.

---

## (2) IMPROVE — polish / clarity

**[HIGH] Resize proration is unexplained** — `components/customer/ResizePicker.tsx` only says "new price applies at your next renewal" + "power cycle." No upfront/prorated charge for a mid-term upgrade. A customer who prepaid 12/36 months (terms exist in `lib/billing-terms.ts`) gets a larger box for free until renewal. **Fix:** either prorate the upgrade and charge the difference immediately, or clearly explain the billing behavior in the UI.

**[MED] Pricing savings claims are inconsistent/undemonstrated** — homepage badge "Save up to 20% with annual billing" (`app/page.tsx`) vs. correct "Save up to 20% on 3-year terms" on `vps`/`pricing`. Actual discounts: 10% annual, 20% at 36 months (`VPS_TERMS`). The `PricingGrid` badge promises savings but the grid has no term toggle — the only place term pricing appears is the deploy wizard Review step. **Fix:** unify copy to "up to 20% on 3-year terms" and add a monthly/annual toggle to the pricing grid, or drop the badge.

**[MED] DNS manager can't edit records** — `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx` supports add + delete only (`DnsAddForm`, `DnsDeleteButton`). Editing means delete-then-recreate, risking downtime. **Fix:** add inline edit.

**[MED] Customer/admin design drift on a few admin pages** — most admin pages use `PageHeader`, but `app/admin/plans/page.tsx` hand-rolls `<h1 className="mb-6 text-2xl font-bold">` and has no `PageHeader`/stats, feeling unfinished next to the polished `subscriptions`/`billing` pages. **Fix:** bring Plans in line with the shared header/layout.

**[MED] Admin tables lack pagination** — `admin/users`, `admin/servers`, `admin/subscriptions`, `admin/billing`, `admin/invoices` (`take: 200`) render everything with no paging.
